results.title: Dalić: We are worried about the technical mistakes we make
highlights:
Dalić: We are worried about the technical mistakes we make
[...]
# Dalić: We are worried about the technical mistakes we make
[...]
There were a lot of good things in these two friendly matches, but there were also bad things, commented Croatian national football team coach Zlatko Dalić after the 2-1 victory against Slovenia in Varaždin.
[...]
"It was a tough game, lively and aggressive. We had problems with the transition back where the Slovenians were a dangerous threat. We are worried about the opponent's chances, as well as the goal that happened after our mistake. We still have ten days of work and we have to fix that. After all, the important thing is the victory," said Dalić, turning to what he saw after the matches against Belgium and Slovenia.
[...]
"We wanted to get Modrić, Kovačić and Guardiola back into shape through the matches. That was the most important thing for us, and that's not easy because, for example, Kovačić has been out of real football for almost a year. Overall, there were good and bad things in these two matches. We made a lot of technical mistakes, which is not typical of us. We need liveliness and energy, but we have solutions and we know what to do. We are impatiently waiting for the start of the World Cup, where the goal is to get through the group, and after that we will go step by step," concluded Dalić.
[...]
"We needed this win for the atmosphere before going to the World Cup. We also needed it because of the previous defeat to Belgium. Now our journey to the championship will be calmer and we can leave with a smile on our faces. The result was close, but I think we played quite well. We created a lot of chances, and the Slovenians also had some through counterattacks. We have these two systems, we know what we have to do and it is up to the coach to decide when to apply which one. We will analyze these two matches and I know that we will be ready for the World Cup. A goal? A goal always means something, especially when it brings victory and raises the atmosphere," said Mario Pašalić after the match, while Martin Erlić also commented on the match with satisfaction.
[...]
"This victory is important for us to continue our preparations for the championship. Now we will have even more motivation to continue. We are on the right track and will be ready for the first match at the World Cup against England. We had some small mistakes in defense, but the mistakes are there to be fixed. Maybe we lacked a little concentration, but we deserved to win. The atmosphere in the team is, as always, great," said Erlić.

results.title: Dalić: I'm very pleased with how we trained
highlights:
The Croatian national football team has completed its final training session during the Rijeka preparations. The Firebirds still have to play a Sunday friendly match against Slovenia in Varaždin before heading to the World Cup, and coach Zlatko Dalić is satisfied with what has been done.
[...]
"The last training session has been completed, the first cycle ends tomorrow. I am very pleased with how we trained. The result against Belgium was not good and that disturbed us a bit. We wanted to give everyone minutes, we wanted to get three players back into shape through the game, Kovačić, Modrić and Guardiola. There is no drama, France and the Netherlands also lost. Everyone is making ten substitutions, this is the last chance to try all the players. Everything is great. We will go 4-2-3-1, we are changing the system. Overall, I am pleased," said Dalić, referring to the change in system.
[...]
"That was the plan. Nothing made me do that and I have no doubts. We learned from Belgium and we do what we do. You have known my system for nine years and we have won two medals. The hierarchy is very important to me, this is not a club, this is a national team. Form is important and that is why we will try more players. There is no room for questioning my work and my logic, the results prove it. This is not a club, but a national team. I stick to my principles and what has led to the results for me and Croatia," said the coach.
[...]
"We're getting the players back into rhythm, they're working well and that's important. We want to get them back in shape, but if they're not at the peak of their abilities, we have alternatives. Vušković is fair, he's working well, he's top in training. He has a guard in him so that the pressure doesn't eat him," added Dalić, announcing tomorrow's match against Slovenia.
[...]
"A match that gives us a chance to try new things. We're looking at the matches against Ghana and Panama to see if we'll play different systems there, and we're looking at the match against Slovenia as a good motivation for us. The Slovenians will try to cause us problems, we'll try to be real."
[...]
"Sučić was paired with Luka and it worked well. Against Belgium, we pushed him alongside Baturina because they are younger and more agile. Petar is a versatile player, he is only growing and is good. Luka Sučić has a great left foot, he is technically phenomenal. He has a place in the national team, we put him on the left flank, we need to improve his defense, but he is always ready and works well," said Dalić, adding that Toni Fruk "even though he had bad luck with his hand injury, he is unquestionable and will get his minutes."

results.title: Croatia to test new formation against Belgium on Tuesday in World Cup warm-up | Croatia Week
highlights:
RIJEKA, 1 June 2026 – Croatia will continue preparations for the FIFA World Cup when they host Belgium in an international friendly in Rijeka on Tuesday evening, with kick-off scheduled for 6 pm.
[...]
Speaking at a pre-match press conference, Croatia head coach Zlatko Dalić described the match as an important test against a strong opponent.
[...]
“We have had several good training sessions together. Belgium are a quality opponent with a number of dangerous players. It is a real test for us and a chance to see where we are. It may be a friendly, but the result is still important,” he said.
[...]
Dalić said Croatia will start in a 3-4-2-1 formation as he head coach experiments with tactical options ahead of the World Cup.
[...]
“We’ll start in a 3-4-2-1 formation, that’s my wish and we’ll try that. It’s a friendly, but the result is important,” he said.
[...]
Dalić’s preferred and most commonly used setup throughout his tenure since 2017 has been 4-2-3-1.
[...]
The coach acknowledged that key players Joško Gvardiol and Mateo Kovačić, who both returned recently from serious injuries, would start the match, along with Luka Modrić, but said the match would provide opportunities for younger squad members who have impressed and there would be a lot of substitutions made.
[...]
The Croatian coach believes Belgium are once again becoming one of the world’s leading sides following a period of transition after Qatar 2022.
[...]
“They were ranked number one in the world under Roberto Martínez and then experienced a slight decline. Now they are returning with new players emerging, such as Jérémy Doku, and a new coach. They have quality and are moving back towards the top level,” he said.
[...]
Dalić also addressed the challenging weather conditions expected during the World Cup in the United States, particularly in Dallas, where high temperatures could present difficulties for players.
[...]
Dalić highlighted the importance of balancing experience with youth, pointing to Croatia’s success at previous World Cups.
[...]
“Experience has brought us a lot in both 2018 and 2022, but younger players are also coming through. We have seen players such as Sučić, Baturina and Vušković emerge. The balance between experienced and younger players is important,” he said.
[...]
will also see midfielder Mario Pašalić make his 100th appearance for his country.
[...]
“Mario deserves to enter the 100-cap club more than anyone. Whenever needed, he played in positions that were not natural to him. Since joining us after 2018, he has always been available and never complained. It is recognition for everything he has done for the team,” Dalić said.

results.title: Zlatko Dalic | Luka Modric | Croatia | FIFA World Cup 2026
highlights:
Zlatko Dalic, Andrej Kramaric and Josip Stanisic discuss Croatia's World Cup ambitions and explain why Luka Modric is central to them.
[...]
It is a remarkable return for a nation of fewer than four million people and has inevitably raised expectations ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026™. Yet while Croatia arrive in Canada, Mexico and the United States with another talented squad, coach Zlatko Dalic has insisted his players are focused on enjoying the occasion rather than being burdened by the achievements of previous generations.

When the Croatia coach was asked to explain the team's success, the conversation repeatedly returned to one man: Luka Modric. The Croatia captain is preparing for a fifth World Cup, joining an exclusive group of players that includes Lothar Matthaus, Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi.
[...]
“Modric is still the main player for this team, the driving force for the national team, the player who keeps the team running,” Dalic admitted. “I think Luka Modric means a lot to this team, which he has already shown many times with his dedication, devotion, performances and behaviour.
[...]
“He is an utmost professional who performs his job at the highest possible level. Although he is 40 years old now, he is still extremely ambitious and is the main driving force behind this national team.”
[...]
Croatia striker Andrej Kramaric believes Modric's influence extends far beyond matchdays, with the veteran midfielder continuing to set the standard for those around him.
[...]
Croatia defender Josip Stanisic echoed the sentiments of his coach and team-mate. “Modric is very important,” Stanisic said. “We can be very happy that he’s still with us. He’s still a top player, even at 40. We know what he can bring to the table. I think our opponents also look at us differently when he’s playing.
[...]
While Modric remains Croatia's driving force, Dalic is determined that the team's ambitions in North America are not overshadowed by the weight of expectation.
[...]
While Kramaric highlights the influence of Croatia's trailblazers, Stanisic believes the current squad's greatest strength lies elsewhere.
[...]
With England, Panama and Ghana awaiting in Group L, Dalic knows Croatia will need to hit the ground running if they are to challenge for another deep run in North America.
[...]
“We want to give our maximum out on the pitch, which was clearly shown at the last two FIFA World Cups. Croatia has the strength and capability to perform well, and I sincerely hope that we will be able to show that.”
